title: Air Ambulance Medical Payload Optimization
real_world_story: An air ambulance helicopter is being dispatched to a remote mountain disaster zone. The helicopter has a strict maximum cargo weight capacity of W kg. Relief workers have prepared N discrete medical kits (such as field trauma surgical sets, portable blood refrigeration units, and pediatric stabilization kits). Kit i has a gross weight of w_i kg and an evaluated clinical utility score of v_i. Kits are sealed and indivisible—each kit must either be completely loaded or left behind. Determine the maximum clinical utility score that can be transported without exceeding weight W.
problem_statement: Given capacity W and N items, where item i has weight w_i and utility value v_i, find the maximum total utility value achievable by selecting a subset of items such that the sum of their weights does not exceed W. Each item can be selected at most once.
task: Compute the maximum total utility score achievable within the helicopter weight capacity W.
input_format:
The first line contains two space-separated integers N and W, the number of kits and the maximum payload capacity.
The next N lines each contain two space-separated integers w_i and v_i, the weight and utility score of the i-th kit.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum total utility score.

examples.explanation: Selecting kit 2 (weight 20, utility 100) and kit 3 (weight 30, utility 120) yields total weight 20 + 30 = 50 <= 50 and total utility 100 + 120 = 220. Selecting all three exceeds capacity (60 > 50). Maximum utility is 220.
All kits exceed the total capacity of 10 kg. No kit can be loaded, yielding total utility 0.

real_world_takeaway: 0/1 Knapsack dynamic programming guarantees the optimal packing of indivisible life-support equipment under rigid aeronautical payload limits.
